signals.title: USD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Spread
signals.text: USD outperforms across G10 with a 1W average gain of +0.634% across 9 pairs, while SEK anchors the bottom of the scorecard at -0.615% across 2 pairs, generating a 1.249% leader-to-laggard spread. USD/SEK trades at 9.773, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 9.576/9.592/9.350. The macro driver remains an intact yield advantage, with SOFR at 3.62% against Riksbank policy at 1.75%, while Sweden's Economic Surprise Index sits at a deeply negative -29.2. BEER fair-value modeling indicates USD/SEK is rich at z=+1.67σ, but persistent growth and surprise divergence continue to drive capital into the dollar ahead of key events. Trade bias: Long USD/SEK; broad dollar strength and Swedish macro underperformance sustain the upside. Catalyst: Fed interest rate decision at 18:00 UTC. Risk: A dovish FOMC outcome compresses the G10 spread below 1.20% and triggers profit-taking back toward 9.600.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 155.27, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 157.14/159.40/158.39. SOFR at 3.62% vs TONA at 0.98% maintains a +264bp carry advantage for the dollar, keeping structural carry demand active while VIX at 17.2 signals normal market volatility. However, options positioning reveals sharp downside hedging, with 25d risk reversals showing a strong put skew of -1.98 as traders brace for central bank risk. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY at -53,255 contracts (pctl 30), reflecting reduced short exposure following a +58,042 WoW cover. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; intact carry premium supports spot while VIX remains contained below 25. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision on 18 Sep. Risk: Hawkish BoJ repricing or a break above VIX 25 triggers rapid carry unwinds toward 153.50.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Policy Spread + CPI Event Risk
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3480, positioning below its SMA20/50 cluster at 1.3557/1.3484 while remaining above the 200-day moving average at 1.3455. Short-term rates favor sterling slightly, with SONIA at 3.7307% vs SOFR at 3.6200% providing a 11bp carry advantage. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net long position of +40,361 contracts, which places positioning at the 86th percentile of its 52-week range (z=+1.02), indicating a stretched institutional long stance after a -7,143 WoW reduction. Realized 30-day volatility sits at 3.5% against 1M implied volatility of 5.4%, creating a +1.9% vol risk premium ahead of critical UK inflation data and central bank announcements. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish GBP/USD; stretched speculative longs leave cable vulnerable if domestic inflation figures underperform. Catalyst: UK CPI release at 06:00 UTC. Risk: A hotter-than-expected UK CPI print forces hawkish BoE repricing, pushing price above 1.3550.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT Extreme + Elevated Options VRP
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7130, holding below its 20-day SMA at 0.7172 but above the 50-day and 200-day SMAs at 0.7077 and 0.7008. Leveraged Funds net long positioning stands at +48,379 contracts, placing it at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range (z=+1.72), marking an extreme spec long bias. Options markets reflect heavy protection demand, with 1M ATM implied volatility running at 7.5% versus 30-day realized volatility at 5.4%, yielding an elevated +2.1% Vol Risk Premium alongside a -0.75 25d risk reversal put skew. RBA Cash Rate at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% provides a +60bp nominal policy rate cushion, though AUD real yields remain mildly accommodative at -0.55% due to 4.90% inflation expectations. Trade bias: Neutral/downside caution AUD/USD; extreme institutional long positioning limits additional upside momentum. Catalyst: US Retail Sales at 12:30 UTC followed by the FOMC Decision at 18:00 UTC. Risk: WoW spec adds resume and push spot back above 0.7175, invalidating the positioning exhaustion read.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Retail Extreme Divergence + Fair Value
signals.text: EUR/CHF trades at 0.9452, supported by a significant interest rate carry advantage of +265bp with ECB policy at 2.65% against SNB policy at 0.00%. Retail trader positioning on Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 89% short bias (11% long), reflecting strong retail fading of the underlying policy differential. Speculative positioning in futures shows CHF net short at -13,968 contracts (pctl 12, z=-1.09), confirming institutional alignment with the carry backdrop rather than the retail short crowd. Cross-asset fair value metrics place EUR/CHF near model parity, while options skew remains mild at -0.44. Trade bias: Long EUR/CHF; structural carry advantage and extreme retail short positioning favor continued upside. Catalyst: SNB interest rate decision on 24 Sep. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment sparks safe-haven flows into CHF, overriding the carry differential.
